findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category/uncategorized_category_id were never explicitly saved to site_settings
findings.body: The migration does `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. SiteSetting rows are only persisted to the `site_settings` table when an admin explicitly changes a value away from its default; on virtually every installation that never customized `embed_category` (default '') there is no matching row, so the query returns zero rows and `result[0]` is nil. Calling `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The same problem exists for the fallback query at lines 14-16 for `uncategorized_category_id` (default -1, also usually unset). Since both guards are missing (unlike the properly-guarded `embeddable_hosts` query a few lines below), this migration will fail to run on most real databases, blocking deploy of this feature entirely.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError instead of 404 for unknown id
findings.body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; save_host(host)` and `destroy` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; host.destroy`. If no record matches `params[:id]` (e.g. stale client state, double-submission, or a race with another admin deleting the host), `host` is nil and the subsequent `host.host = ...` or `host.destroy` call raises NoMethodError, resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of a clean 404/error response.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil/blank
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is nil (e.g. the `embeddable_host` param is missing or explicitly blank when creating/updating a host via the admin controller, which assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError before the format validation ever runs, turning what should be a normal validation failure into an unhandled 500 error.

findings.title: Host lookup is only half case-insensitive, can fail to match
findings.body: `record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, lower-casing only the database column but not the `host` variable used for comparison (`host = uri.host`, which preserves whatever case the referer/embed URL used, e.g. 'MySite.com'). If the stored host or the inbound host differs only in case, the match fails even though the intent is clearly to be case-insensitive. This can cause legitimate embeds to be rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Existing tests only use all-lowercase hosts, so this gap is not covered.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents were swapped with embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) that used to live here were moved into the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The file names no longer match their contents (the Fabrication gem loads all files regardless of name, so tests still pass, but this is clearly an accidental swap that will confuse anyone looking for category or embeddable_host fabricators by filename) and should be corrected before merge.

findings.title: Host format validation rejects many legitimate modern TLDs
findings.body: `validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` restricts the TLD portion to 2-5 letters. Many valid gTLDs in use since well before 2015 are longer than 5 characters (e.g. `.company`, `.technology`, `.community`), so hosts using them will be rejected as invalid even though they are perfectly legitimate domains, limiting the usability of this new admin feature.

findings.title: Migration builds INSERT via unescaped string interpolation
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` interpolates the previous `embeddable_hosts` setting value directly into raw SQL without quoting/escaping. If any historical value contains a single quote or other SQL-significant character, the migration will fail with a syntax error (or, in the worst case, execute unintended SQL). `connection.quote(h)` (or a parameterized execute) should be used instead.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host allows duplicate records
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost` has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive). The admin UI and controller allow creating multiple `EmbeddableHost` rows with the same host value pointing at different categories; `record_for_host`/`host_allowed?` will silently pick whichever one happens to be returned first by the DB, giving inconsistent/undefined category routing for topic embeds without any error or warning to the admin.

findings.title: find embedded test does not actually exercise the requested id
findings.body: The 'find embedded' test was changed from `store.find('fruit', 1)` to `store.find('fruit', 2)`, asserting that the result's `colors` are ids `[1, 2]`. However, the `/fruits/:id` pretender route in create-pretender.js.es6 is unchanged and always returns `fruits[0]` (the apple record with color_ids `[1,2]`) regardless of the requested id. Fruit id 2 (banana) actually only has `color_ids: [3]` in the fixture data. The test therefore passes only because the mock server ignores the id parameter, not because the embedded-ids hydration logic was verified against the record it claims to fetch; a real regression in id-based lookups would go undetected by this test.

findings.title: embeddable_hosts resource routes lack matching controller actions
findings.body: `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` generates the full set of RESTful routes (index, new, show, edit, in addition to create/update/destroy), but `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only implements `create`, `update`, and `destroy`. Requests to the unimplemented routes (index/show/new/edit) will raise `AbstractController::ActionNotFound` rather than a clean 404, which is unnecessary attack surface/noise for routes that are never used by the UI; `resources :embeddable_hosts, only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` would be more correct.
